objective: Prove that over corner variables (each the agreement of a corner's two literals, a 2-XOR) the sphere's count has a cutting-planes refutation of linear size, while every corner parity it states holds under every assignment; so cutting planes lacks only the corner atoms and Res(xor) has the atoms but needs to count them, locating the two open cells.
status: Proved 2026-11-10: over corner atoms (2-XORs of points, defined by four clauses each) cutting planes refutes the sphere's count with O(n) lines (lines give sum <= 1, faces sum >= 1, F - L = 2); every corner parity holds under every assignment, so the contradiction is an integer count invisible modulo 2; over the points alone the LP is feasible at x = 1/2.
title: The count is a linear count of corner parities
